symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Each \(e\in E\) indexes one randomized two-arm trial.

symbols.name: l_e
symbols.def: \(l_e\) is the left endpoint of edge \(e\).

symbols.name: r_e
symbols.def: \(r_e\) is the right endpoint of edge \(e\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G=(V,E)\), with edge orientations used to sign contrasts and to select the left-endpoint anchor for the support-tangent lift.

symbols.name: Zcal_e
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z_e\) is the support of \(Z_e\) for each \(e\in E\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A public upper bound on latent support size.

symbols.name: Scal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal S=\{0\}\cup E\), where \(S=0\) denotes the target and \(S=e\) denotes trial \(e\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: A law for \((S,X,U,W,(Z_e)_{e\in E},A,Y_a,Y)\) on the declared finite supports.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: \(P=\operatorname{obs}(Q)\) is the collection of trial laws of \((A,Y,X,W,Z_e)\) and the target law of \((X,W)\).

symbols.name: M_L_eta
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\) is the finite tangent-rich proximal trial-network class defined in \(\text{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: A lower bound for each complete observed cell probability.

symbols.name: n_s
symbols.def: \(n_s\) is the sample size in population \(s\in\mathcal S\).

symbols.name: Gamma_K
symbols.def: For each \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{anc}}\), \(\Gamma_{s,x,u,w,a}:D_a\to\{\xi:\operatorname{supp}(\xi)\subseteq\mathcal Y^+_{s,x,u,w},\ \sum_y\xi(y)=0\}\) is a fixed linear map satisfying \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\Gamma_{s,x,u,w,a}d=d\).

symbols.name: g_a
symbols.def: \(g_0(w,x)=0\), and \(g_a(w,x)\) indexes the bridge contrast at node \(a\).

symbols.name: B_e
symbols.def: \(B_e\) is the signed incidence row of \((l_e,r_e)\) after deleting the root column.

symbols.name: J_e
symbols.def: \(J_e\) injects an edge-indexed vector over \((x,z)\) into the corresponding coordinates of the stack defining \(b_P\).

symbols.name: A_p
symbols.def: For each candidate observed table \(p\), \(A_p\) is obtained from the formula for \(A_P\) with every primitive cell probability evaluated under \(p\).

symbols.name: b_p
symbols.def: For each candidate observed table \(p\), \(b_p\) is obtained from the formula for \(b_P\) with every primitive cell probability evaluated under \(p\).

symbols.name: R_p
symbols.def: For each candidate observed table \(p\), \((R_p g)_a=\sum_{x,w}p(X=x,W=w\mid S=0)g_a(w,x)\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h=(h_a(w,x))\) is an arbitrary element of \(\ker(A_P)\), with \(h_0=0\).

symbols.name: a_s
symbols.def: \(a_0=0\) and \(a_e=l_e\) for each trial population \(e\in E\).

symbols.name: epsilon_star
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_*(h)=\min_{\Delta^h_{s,x,u,w}(y)\ne0}K_{s,x,u,w}(y)/|\Delta^h_{s,x,u,w}(y)|\), with the empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\); finiteness of the index set and support restriction of \(\Delta^h\) make every nonempty ratio strictly positive.

symbols.name: Q_epsilon_h
symbols.def: \(Q^{\varepsilon,h}\) keeps every component of \(Q\) fixed except that \(K_{s,x,u,w}\) is replaced by \(K_{s,x,u,w}+\varepsilon\Delta^h_{s,x,u,w}\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: In a fixed covariate stratum \(x\), write \(q=q_x=\operatorname{rank}(C_x)\).

symbols.name: eta0
symbols.def: A strict lower margin for latent mixtures and their induced proxy rows.

symbols.name: t_e
symbols.def: In the rank-one submodel, \(t_e\) is the common row of \(T_{e,x}\) for edge \(e\).

symbols.name: mu_C
symbols.def: \(\mu_C\) is product relative Lebesgue measure on \(O_C(\eta_0)^E\), with the zero-dimensional point mass convention when \(q=1\).

symbols.name: treepack_q
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{TreePack}_q(G)\) holds when \(G\) contains \(q\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees.

symbols.name: c_F
symbols.def: \(c(F)\) is the number of connected components of the spanning multigraph \((V,F)\).

symbols.name: E_plus
symbols.type: finite multiset of candidate added trial edges
symbols.def: \(E^+\) is the prespecified menu of randomized comparisons available for network augmentation, disjoint from the labeled edge multiset \(E\).

symbols.name: c_plus
symbols.def: \(c^+(e)\) is the cost of adding candidate trial edge \(e\).

symbols.name: F_star
symbols.def: \(F_*\in\arg\min_{F\subseteq E^+}\{\sum_{e\in F}c^+(e):r_q(E\cup F)=q(|V|-1)\}\), when the feasible family is nonempty.

symbols.name: E_example
symbols.type: fully specified two-stratum proximal network instance
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak E\) has \(L=2\), \(\eta_0=1/16\), \(\eta=1/1000\), \(V=\{0,1,2,3\}\), \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,x_2\}\), \(\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\{1,2\}\), \(P(X=x_j\mid S=s)=1/2\), \(C_{x_1}=\begin{psmallmatrix}3/4&1/4\\1/4&3/4\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(C_{x_2}=\begin{psmallmatrix}1/2&1/2\\1/2&1/2\end{psmallmatrix}\), and ordered edges \(01,12,23,02,03,13\); at \(x_1\), edge \(j\) has latent mixture \((j/8,1-j/8)\), while at \(x_2\) every mixture is \((1/2,1/2)\). The target mixtures are \((7/8,1/8)\) at \(x_1\) and \((1/2,1/2)\) at \(x_2\). Every \(Z_e\) has singleton support. Every conditional potential-outcome kernel puts mass \(1/5\) on \(0000,1000,0100,0010,0001\) and zero elsewhere, the shared bridge is \(g_a(w,x)=0\), and treatment is balanced within every trial.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: The common value \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A_P)\) on a separated-rank class.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega\) is fixed or a twice continuously differentiable positive-definite function of the primitive cell probabilities.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: A lower bound for the smallest retained singular value.

symbols.name: theta_hat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta=\widehat R_0\widehat M_{P,\kappa/2}^{+}\widehat\Omega^{1/2}\widehat b_P\), where only singular values above \(\kappa/2\) are retained.

symbols.name: M_total
symbols.def: The number of complete observed multinomial cells across all populations in \(\mathcal S\).

symbols.name: K_sj
symbols.def: \(K_{sj}\) is the count in complete cell \(j\) of population \(s\).

symbols.name: C_n_P
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_n^P\) is \(B_n\) intersected with normalized nonnegative tables, the \(\eta\)-cell restriction, and known trial randomization constraints.

symbols.name: F_P
symbols.def: When it exists, \(F_P\) is any matrix satisfying \(F_PA_P=R_0\).

symbols.name: support_face_handle
symbols.def: Start from the positive support of each \(K_{s,x,u,w}\) and the range of its marginal tangent map \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\), solve the coupled observed-cell equations without dividing by zero entries of \(C_x\), compute the resulting feasible two-sided tangent cone of the observed-law fiber, and dualize it by finite-dimensional Farkas separation.

assumptions.condition: The alphabets \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal W\), and \(\mathcal Z_e\) are finite for every \(e\in E\).

novel.justification: A public support bound is credible when the latent modifier is a finite clinical severity type or a prespecified coarsening of a finite baseline profile; it prevents a necessity witness from hiding support enlargement.

assumptions.condition: \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely in every trial population.

novel.justification: The condition holds for finite latent-class mixtures in which each prespecified severity type occurs in every harmonized trial population; it excludes population-specific deletion of a latent type while allowing arbitrarily different mixing weights.

assumptions.condition: \(C_x(w\mid u)>0\) for every \((x,u,w)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\).

novel.justification: Strict proxy positivity is realistic for coarsened noisy assays whose categories all have nonzero misclassification probability within each latent class; it leaves rank unrestricted while excluding support faces.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s,x,u,w\), the anchor-zero subspace \(D_{a_s}\) is contained in the range of the one-way marginal tangent map \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\).

novel.justification: This local support condition asks only for the population's anchor-zero marginal increments used by the lift, allows structural zeros, and holds whenever the positive support contains the all-zero atom and the \(k+1\) single-one atoms. It is a property of the primitive conditional outcome law and the prespecified trial endpoints, not of an estimator or of the target nullspace.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(a\in V\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(u\in\mathcal U\), \(\mathbb E_Q[Y(a)-Y(0)\mid X=x,U=u,S=s]=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}C_x(w\mid u)g_a(w,x)\).

novel.justification: The restriction allows arbitrary population-specific baseline risks and transports only treatment-node contrasts. It is natural for harmonized trials in which latent effect modification is shared while prognostic levels and latent mixtures differ.

assumptions.condition: Every complete observed cell probability under \(P\) is at least \(\eta\).

novel.justification: This restriction isolates the empirically relevant regime in which no single randomized comparison has enough proxy variation for full bridge recovery, so identification must be collective across the network.

assumptions.condition: The underlying undirected multigraph of \(G\) is connected.
For the design theorem, every row of \(T_{e,x}\) equals an edge-specific vector \(t_e\in O_C(\eta_0)\) in the fixed stratum \(x\).

novel.justification: The submodel describes trials whose treatment-side proxy does not refine the observed distribution of the adjustment proxy after conditioning on the covariate stratum; edge-to-edge latent mixtures still generate distinct attainable rows.

definitions.name: Finite tangent-rich proximal trial-network class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}=\{(Q,P,G,\mathcal X,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,(\mathcal Z_e)_{e\in E}):\text{every member property listed below holds for all }e\in E,\ s\in\mathcal S,\ x\in\mathcal X,\ u\in\mathcal U,\ w\in\mathcal W,\ a\in V\}\).

definitions.name: Universal signed-cell lift
definitions.construction: Given \(h\in\ker(A_P)\), form \(r^h\), choose positive \(\rho_x\), set \(d^h_{s,a}=\rho_x(r^h_a-r^h_{a_s})/C_x\), apply the fixed anchor-specific support-tangent map \(\Gamma_{s,x,u,w,a_s}\), set \(\Delta^h=\Gamma_{s,x,u,w,a_s}(d^h)\) on the positive support of \(K\), and replace \(K\) by \(K+\varepsilon\Delta^h\) for \(|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_*(h)\).

definitions.name: Attainable rank-\(q\) row domain
definitions.construction: \(O_C(\eta_0)=\{\pi^{\mathsf T}C_x:\sum_u\pi_u=1,\ \pi_u>\eta_0,\ (\pi^{\mathsf T}C_x)_w>\eta_0\ \forall u,w\}\), equipped edgewise with \(\mu_C\).

definitions.name: Classical graphic-matroid union certificate
definitions.construction: Apply the classical tree-packing and matroid-union results of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and \cite{Edmonds1965} to compute \(r_q(E)\), disjoint forests \((F_1,\ldots,F_q)\), and a minimizing set in the union-rank formula involving \(c(F)\).

definitions.name: Minimum-cost attainable-rank augmentation
definitions.construction: Given \(G\), fixed-stratum rank \(q\), candidate edges \(E^+\), and costs \(c^+\), compute \(F_*\) by weighted graphic-matroid union subject to \(r_q(E\cup F_*)=q(|V|-1)\).

definitions.name: Bonferroni exact causal projection
definitions.construction: Set \(\delta=\alpha/M_{\mathrm{total}}\), form every closed Clopper--Pearson interval \(I_{sj}(\delta)\), intersect their product with normalized \(\eta\)-positive randomized tables to obtain \(\mathcal C_n^P\), and project \(\{(p,g):p\in\mathcal C_n^P,\ A_p g=b_p\}\) through \((p,g)\mapsto R_p g\), where \(A_p,b_p,R_p\) are evaluated at the same candidate table \(p\).

definitions.name: Two-stratum four-treatment threshold example
definitions.construction: Use the fully specified instance \(\mathfrak E\). Before edge \(13\) is added, the \(x_1\) effective operator has the null vector with node rows \(h_1=(44,-20)\), \(h_2=(-16,16)\), and \(h_3=(-7,9)\), while \(h=0\) at \(x_2\). The five-atom outcome support has the explicit right inverse \(\Gamma(d)(0000)=-\sum_{a=0}^3d_a\), \(\Gamma(d)(1000)=d_0\), \(\Gamma(d)(0100)=d_1\), \(\Gamma(d)(0010)=d_2\), and \(\Gamma(d)(0001)=d_3\). Add edge \(13\) with its sixth attainable row to obtain the two tree decomposition \(\{01,12,23\}\cup\{02,03,13\}\).

definitions.name: Support-face tangent-cone route
definitions.construction: Restrict signed outcome perturbations to \(\mathcal Y^+_{s,x,u,w}\), retain only increments in the range of \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\), impose the coupled observed-cell equations directly when \(C_x\) has zeros, and use Farkas duality to obtain the annihilator of the resulting two-sided causal-completion tangent cone.

statements.statement: For every \((Q,P)\in\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\), the shared bridge satisfies \(A_Pg=b_P\) and the causal target satisfies \(\theta=R_0g\). Consequently, \(H(P)\ne\varnothing\).
statements.justification: This is the observable reduction that separates bridge algebra from the harder causal necessity direction.
statements.gap: Su et al. derive the two-trial bridge formula; the stacked multigraph operator and target map are not stated there.
statements.consumer: It gives network analysts a finite linear system whose solutions encode every causally admissible root contrast.

statements.statement: Fix \((Q,P)\in\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\) and \(h\in\ker(A_P)\). The support-tangent right inverses produce \(\Delta^h\) with zero total mass and one-way marginal increment \(d^h\). Moreover \(\varepsilon_*(h)>0\), because every nonzero coordinate of \(\Delta^h\) lies on a positive atom of the finite kernel \(K\). For every \(|\varepsilon|<\varepsilon_*(h)\), \(Q^{\varepsilon,h}\in\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\) has observed law \(P\), the same latent support, proxy kernels, and assignment mechanism as \(Q\), admits bridge \(g+\varepsilon h\), and has target \(\theta(Q^{\varepsilon,h})=\theta(Q)+\varepsilon R_0h\).
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing causal lift: it turns every algebraic null direction into actual indistinguishable causal laws.
statements.gap: Proposition 2.3 of \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023} varies statistical solutions to an integral equation but does not construct finite full-data laws preserving an entire trial network and latent contrast restrictions. The support-tangent formulation also avoids assuming positivity of unneeded joint potential-outcome atoms.
statements.consumer: It certifies that a failed nullspace test in a proximal evidence network reflects genuine causal ambiguity, not an artifact of bridge parametrization.

statements.statement: For every observed law \(P\) compatible with \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\), \(\theta\) is point identified over all compatible full-data laws if and only if \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), equivalently \(\nu(P)=0\), equivalently there exists \(F_P\) with \(F_PA_P=R_0\). In that event \(\theta=F_Pb_P\). This strictly strengthens the bridge-fiber criterion in Proposition 2.3 of \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023} on the finite tangent-rich causal model because the necessity direction is witnessed by full causal completions, while its purely statistical criterion is recovered by forgetting those completions.
statements.justification: The equivalence is the paper's exact identification frontier and yields an observable formula whenever identification holds.
statements.gap: The closest published result is Zhang et al.'s annihilator condition for a linear functional of a statistical bridge solution; causal realizability of every violating direction and simultaneous preservation across randomized edges are absent.
statements.consumer: NETMOTION investigators can determine which oxygen-level risk differences are point identified without requiring recovery of the full bridge.

statements.statement: For any tangent-rich completion \(Q\) of \(P\), the compatible target set contains a relatively open neighborhood of \(\theta(Q)\) in \(\theta(Q)+R_0\ker(A_P)\), and this affine space has dimension \(\nu(P)\).
statements.justification: The result upgrades a binary identified-or-not verdict to a local dimension of causal ambiguity.
statements.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge results do not give a causal local-dimension statement for the observed-law fiber.
statements.consumer: Designers can rank candidate data additions by the number of target-relevant ambiguity directions they remove.

statements.statement: For every compatible completion \(Q\), trial \(e\), and covariate stratum \(x\), \(T_{e,x}=H^Q_{e,x}C_x\). Therefore \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x})\le q_x(|V|-1)\le\min\{L,d\}(|V|-1)\) for each \(x\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_P)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x})\le(|V|-1)\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_x\).
statements.justification: The ceiling distinguishes information supplied by more treatment comparisons from information absent because the common proxy kernel is low rank.
statements.gap: Miao et al. make proxy rank central in one proximal problem but do not tensor that ceiling with a treatment-incidence network.
statements.consumer: Trial planners can rule out futile edge additions when proxy rank, rather than network connectivity, is binding.

statements.statement: Fix a stratum \(x\), a positive common kernel \(C_x\) of rank \(q=q_x\), and nonempty \(O_C(\eta_0)\). Under the rank-one row submodel, \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x})=q(|V|-1)\) for \(\mu_C\)-almost every edge-row collection if and only if \(\operatorname{TreePack}_q(G)\) holds. The exceptional deficient collections are the zero set of the maximal minors of \(A_{P,x}\) in relative coordinates on \(H_C^E\). Consequently, across strata the generic global rank is \(\sum_x q_x(|V|-1)\) exactly when \(G\) packs \(q_x\) spanning trees for every \(x\).
statements.justification: This theorem proves that rows genuinely attainable from a common stochastic proxy kernel realize the classical tree-packing threshold, stratum by stratum.
statements.gap: The tree-packing and matroid-union certificates are classical. The new step is the nonvanishing representation theorem for constrained stochastic rows in the common-proxy image, followed by its causal rank interpretation.
statements.consumer: A network designer can identify the least connectivity structure capable of attaining every contrast direction allowed by the proxies.

statements.statement: As a classical corollary of the graphic-matroid union theorem in \cite{Edmonds1965}, \(r_q(E)=\min_{F\subseteq E}\{|E\setminus F|+q(|V|-c(F))\}\). Applied after the attainable-row theorem and the tree-packing criterion of \cite{NashWilliams1961}, its disjoint-forest and minimizing-set outputs certify whether the causal operator can generically attain rank \(q(|V|-1)\); no new combinatorial min--max theorem is claimed.
statements.justification: The cited classical certificate makes the new causal rank conclusion auditable without treating the certificate itself as a contribution.
statements.gap: The min--max identity is classical; the only project-specific content is that Theorem 6 makes it a certificate for attainable proximal-network rank.
statements.consumer: Evidence-network curators can attach a short classical certificate to the causal conclusion that a proposed graph does or does not exhaust its proxy-limited information.

statements.statement: Fix a stratum of common-proxy rank \(q\). If the candidate menu contains a set \(F\) with \(r_q(E\cup F)=q(|V|-1)\), then adding the minimum-cost set \(F_*\) makes \(A_{P,x}\) attain rank \(q(|V|-1)\) for almost every attainable row collection. If this saturation holds in every stratum, then \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), so all target root contrasts \(\theta\) are generically identified for every compatible target latent mixture. Every feasible augmentation uses at least \(q(|V|-1)-r_q(E)\) new labeled trial edges in the fixed stratum, and equality holds whenever the menu contains an extension of a maximum union-independent set. If no such \(F\) exists, no choice of trials from the menu can remove the corresponding generic causal rank deficit.
statements.justification: This is the novel causal design output: a certified trial addition is translated into attainable information rank, and an infeasible menu is declared causally futile.
statements.gap: Weighted matroid augmentation is classical, but existing treatment-network design does not certify which additions exhaust the information attainable under a shared low-rank proxy kernel.
statements.consumer: NETMOTION planners can distinguish a missing randomized comparison that completes the proxy-limited design from additions that leave the same causal ambiguity dimension.

statements.statement: In the instance \(\mathfrak E\), the five-edge graph obtained by omitting \(13\) has \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x_1})=5<6\) and the displayed null vector satisfies \(R_0h=(12,-3,-1)^{\mathsf T}\). Its five-atom outcome support satisfies the support-tangent assumption although eleven of sixteen joint atoms have zero probability; the signed-cell lift therefore gives a nonzero two-sided interval of observationally equivalent completions whose targets differ by \(\varepsilon(12,-3,-1)^{\mathsf T}\). Adding trial \(13\) yields two edge-disjoint spanning trees and generic ranks \(6\) at \(x_1\), \(3\) at \(x_2\), and \(9\) globally. The root contrasts are then identified although the \(x_2\) bridge is not fully recoverable because \(q_{x_2}=1<d=2\). Thus this instance lies beyond the full-rank finite-proxy guarantee of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} and beyond the single indirect-comparison topology of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}; observed-modifier transport in \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} also does not certify it because the effect modifier is latent.
statements.justification: The example simultaneously tests structural outcome zeros, an explicit target-relevant null direction, heterogeneous stratum ranks, and the exact two-tree augmentation threshold.
statements.gap: Published finite-proxy identification, two-trial proximal transport, and observed-modifier multitrial transport each miss at least one defining feature of this explicit law.
statements.consumer: The example is a reproducible template for diagnosing when one additional comparison changes NETMOTION identification rather than merely adding sample size.

statements.statement: In any fixed stratum of the rank-one design submodel, generic recovery of the full \(W\)-indexed bridge holds if and only if \(q_x=d\) and \(\operatorname{TreePack}_d(G)\) holds. If \(q_x<d\), no addition of randomized comparison edges can recover the full bridge in that stratum, although selected target contrasts may still satisfy \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\).
statements.justification: The corollary separates full nuisance recovery from identification of the causal functional.
statements.gap: Finite-proxy rank results do not distinguish graph saturation of effective coordinates from full bridge recovery in a trial network.
statements.consumer: NETMOTION analysts can see why additional trials may identify clinically relevant contrasts without ever identifying every proxy-indexed bridge coordinate.

statements.statement: Uniformly over every compact subset of observed laws from \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\) satisfying \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A_P)=r\), and \(\sigma_r(M_P)\ge\kappa\), the vector \(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta-\theta)\) is asymptotically Gaussian with covariance \(V(P,\lambda)\), the plug-in covariance is uniformly consistent, and the resulting joint Wald ellipsoid has coverage converging uniformly to \(1-\alpha\). The derivative is invariant to the representative \(g_*\).
statements.justification: The theorem supplies ordinary root-\(n\) inference when rank is separated without pretending that the bridge itself is unique.
statements.gap: Bennett et al. and Zhang et al. give regular inference for strongly identified functionals of nonunique nuisances, but not the finite multigraph derivative and its cancellation across a fixed deficient-rank stratum.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain regular finite-dimensional Wald inference in well-conditioned network strata while retaining the exact identification criterion.

statements.statement: For every finite vector of sample sizes and every \(P\) compatible with \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\), \(\Pr_P\{\Theta_I(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n^\theta\}\ge1-\alpha\). The guarantee holds at every rank, including zero cell counts and nonidentified laws, uses no rank selection, and the set \(\mathcal C_n^\theta\) has a terminating semialgebraic description after denominator clearing.
statements.justification: This provides finite-sample coverage of every causally compatible contrast through rank transitions where Wald theory is discontinuous.
statements.gap: Kaido et al. provide uniformly asymptotic calibrated projection, whereas the finite multinomial model permits an exact conservative primitive region whose deterministic projection remains valid without rank regularity.
statements.consumer: Small neonatal trial networks receive honest simultaneous regions even when proxy rank is weak, deficient, or empirically unstable.

statements.statement: When \(C_x\) has zeros or the anchor-zero subspace \(D_{a_s}\) is not contained in the range of \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\), characterize exactly which target directions admit two-sided observationally equivalent causal perturbations and determine whether point identification is equivalent to annihilation of the feasible two-sided tangent cone produced by the support-face route.
statements.justification: Zeros in the common proxy kernel or an outcome support with deficient one-way tangent rank are the boundaries at which the division or two-sided support argument fails, so the tangent-rich theorem does not settle every sparse-proxy case.
statements.gap: Neither the nonunique-bridge literature nor existing proxy bounds characterize the causal tangent cone of a fixed observed-law support face.
statements.consumer: The answer would determine which exact-nullity conclusions survive sparse assay categories and structural zero outcomes instead of requiring artificial smoothing.

sampling_model.design: Independent samples are drawn from one target population and from each edge-indexed randomized trial; in trial \(e\), treatment is assigned with probability \(1/2\) to each endpoint of \(e\).
sampling_model.units: Each trial unit contributes \((A,Y,X,W,Z_e)\), and each target unit contributes \((X,W)\); all alphabets are fixed and finite.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment set is \(V=\{0,\ldots,k\}\), with treatment \(0\) the root and the observed randomized comparisons encoded by a directed multigraph \(G=(V,E)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All observed complete cells are at least \(\eta>0\), and each sampling proportion converges to a positive limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell frequencies estimate each \(A_{P,x}\), the block-diagonal \(A_P\), \(b_P\), and \(R_0\). A fixed spectral cutoff is used only on a separated-rank class; the exact confidence projection evaluates \(A_p,b_p,R_p\) jointly at every candidate table and uses no estimated rank.

Proposition 2 identifies the target contrast from any solution of either observed bridge equation in a two-trial indirect comparison.
The finite-proxy causal effect is identified under a full-rank proxy matrix without identification of the measurement mechanism.
The tree-packing theorem characterizes \(q\) edge-disjoint spanning trees by partition cut inequalities.
The matroid partition theorem gives the classical union-rank min--max formula through disjoint independent sets.
Theorem 1 expresses orthogonally invariant treatment-design criteria through the spectrum of a vertex-weighted graph Laplacian.
A strongly identified linear functional admits root-\(n\) asymptotically normal inference despite a weakly identified conditional-moment nuisance.

tldr: A finite network of randomized treatment comparisons can identify transported root contrasts even when every trial-specific proxy bridge is nonunique. The paper's kernel is a causal nullity theorem: under finite binary outcomes and a support-tangent condition that permits structural zeros, the target vector is identified if and only if \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), and every violation is realized by an explicit two-sided family of observationally equivalent full-data laws. Stratum-specific operators \(A_{P,x}\) make the second headline precise: attainable rows from a rank-\(q_x\) common proxy kernel generically reach rank \(q_x(|V|-1)\) exactly at the \(q_x\)-tree threshold, with global rank equal to the sum across strata. Classical matroid union then certifies a concrete minimum-cost trial augmentation; separated-rank Wald inference and exact candidate-law projection provide complementary uncertainty guarantees.

project_justification.gap: Zhang et al. characterize invariance of a linear functional over a statistical bridge fiber, and Su et al. identify one transported two-trial contrast. Neither result proves that each target-relevant bridge null direction corresponds to two support-feasible causal completions that preserve every observed trial cell and the shared latent contrast restrictions in an arbitrary treatment network.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the causal tangent space of a finite proximal trial network: algebraic nonuniqueness must be lifted through potential-outcome kernels while holding the full observed law fixed. Its dimension and its interaction with treatment-graph connectivity determine which new trials can add causal information.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs a support-restricted signed-cell lift for every null direction, derives the exact annihilator criterion and local ambiguity dimension, and proves that rows attainable from a common stochastic proxy kernel realize the classical tree-packing rank threshold in each stratum. Classical matroid union is used only to certify a new causal network-augmentation consequence. Regular inference on separated rank strata and conservative exact candidate-law projection complete the analysis.

related_work: The affine-solution insight comes from \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023}, whose Proposition 2.3 identifies a linear functional when it annihilates the bridge nullspace; the present kernel addresses the stronger causal question by realizing every violating direction through support-feasible full-data completions. \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026} supplies a two-trial proximal indirect-comparison formula, while the multistratum example has four treatments, cycles, and collective rank unavailable from a single indirect comparison. \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} supplies the finite-proxy matrix-rank perspective, but the example remains contrast-identified in a stratum with \(q_x<d\). \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} transports effects from multiple trials using observed effect modifiers; it does not certify the example with a latent modifier and proxy restrictions. \cite{XuEtAl2026} studies two-trial proximal reconciliation under parametric latent effect-modification models and is informative rather than a theorem-level target. The graph threshold uses the classical tree-packing result of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and the classical matroid-partition result of \cite{Edmonds1965}; neither certificate nor the projection operation is presented as new. \cite{Rosa2018} informs precision design after attainable rank is settled. The separated-rank estimator is informed by \cite{BennettEtAl2023}, and exact Clopper--Pearson cell projection is a conservative finite-sample complement to \cite{KaidoMolinariStoye2019}. \cite{SotiropoulosEtAl2024} supplies the NETMOTION consumer, where a low-rank proxy stratum can bind before additional graph connectivity does.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact causal converse is restricted to finite binary outcomes, a public finite latent-support bound, strictly positive common \(W\)-given-\(U\) kernels, and conditional potential-outcome supports spanning every anchor-zero one-way marginal increment used by the lift. The latter permits structural zeros but excludes support faces with deficient anchor-zero tangent rank. Tree packing, matroid union, and the deterministic projection argument are classical; novelty rests on the support-feasible causal lift, the attainable common-proxy-row representation, and their network-augmentation implication. The exact confidence set may be conservative, nonconvex, or nonshrinking near rank changes.
honest_scope: The support-restricted signed-cell lift, exact nullity equivalence, local ambiguity dimension, attainable common-row rank theorem, multistratum example, causal augmentation consequence, and two inference guarantees are theorem targets. The support-face extension remains open when the one-way support-tangent map is not surjective or the common proxy kernel has zeros. Under one source edge, one target population, and a target functional that annihilates the bridge kernel, the observable formula reduces to the any-solution proximal transport formula of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}. In a stratum with \(q_x=d\) and \(d\) edge-disjoint spanning trees, the graph result reduces to ordinary full-column-rank bridge recovery; with \(q_x<d\), it respects the finite-proxy rank ceiling of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018}. The NETMOTION application is conditional on valid harmonized proxies and an independent target sample.

literature_map: The selected kernel sits at the intersection of proximal nonuniqueness, trial transport, and graph rank. \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} and \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023} establish finite-proxy rank identification and invariance of selected functionals under bridge nonuniqueness. \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026} identifies one proximal indirect comparison, while \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} handles multiple trials through observed modifiers and \cite{XuEtAl2026} remains a two-trial parametric reconciliation framework. \cite{NashWilliams1961} and \cite{Edmonds1965} supply the classical tree-packing and matroid-union certificates, while \cite{Rosa2018} relates ordinary treatment information to graph spectra. The new objects are the support-feasible causal-completion lift and the proof that stochastic rows attainable from one common kernel realize the tree threshold for each \(A_{P,x}\), producing a causal augmentation consequence. \cite{BennettEtAl2023} and \cite{KaidoMolinariStoye2019} inform the supporting inference results.

novelty_justification: The closest identification theorem is Proposition 2.3 of \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023}: a linear functional is constant over a conditional-moment solution set exactly when its representer annihilates the operator nullspace. The exact-nullity theorem recovers that algebra after stacking randomized treatment edges, while the signed-cell theorem supplies the missing causal necessity by mapping every algebraic null vector to two full-data laws preserving all observed cells, the common proxy kernel, and shared latent node contrasts. Its primitive support-tangent condition is strictly weaker than positivity of the entire joint potential-outcome cube and gives an explicit positive radius through a support-restricted right inverse. The second headline is not the classical tree-packing or matroid-partition certificate of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and \cite{Edmonds1965}: it is the representation theorem that rows attainable from a rank-\(q_x\) stochastic common kernel make \(A_{P,x}\) attain \(q_x(|V|-1)\) generically exactly at the tree threshold. The resulting minimum-cost augmentation statement is causal because its certificate determines whether added randomized comparisons remove proxy-limited ambiguity. The explicit two-stratum example is not covered by the full-rank condition of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018}, the two-trial topology of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}, or observed-modifier transport in \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023}.
